Nowy Sacz New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowy Sącz, Poland

Not demolished. Nowy Sącz became one of the region's most important Hasidic centers from the 19th century; by 1921, 9,009 Jews (34%) lived there, mostly killed by German forces in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 19th century, became the burial site in 1876 of Rabbi Chaim Halberstam ('Divrei Chaim'), founder of the Sanz Hasidic dynasty, with subsequent dynasty leaders buried nearby beneath a shared ohel. Germans killed several hundred Jews and Poles here during WWII, causing serious damage; postwar, the County Jewish Committee restored the site, recovering displaced matzevot and rebuilding the ohel. The cemetery continued receiving exhumed Holocaust victims from Limanowa and elsewhere, and remains open for occasional burials today under the Hasidic Bnei Sanz foundation, opposite an active Hasidic center with mikveh and temple.
